prompts.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Asset type: a single polished full rider HOMEPAGE design proposal for Rakky Ride, portrait mobile screen, for approval before coding. No other pages.
Input image 1 is an actual Google Maps screenshot crop of a public road area, without a user's location marker or private details. It is the BACKGROUND MAP REFERENCE. Use these real map pixels as the backdrop, scaling/cropping as needed; preserve road geometry and labels rather than painting invented streets. Do not generate a fake or illustrated map. Show unobscured Google map attribution near the map edge.
Input image 2 is a PREVIOUS DESIGN BOARD used ONLY as the reference for the THREE SERVICE ILLUSTRATIONS in its leftmost panel: the small clean matte GREEN 3D CAR, cardboard COURIER BOX, and white CALENDAR with green binding. Reproduce these same appealing compact stylized 3D objects, not emoji and not realistic photographs. Ignore the rest of that board's layout.
Primary request: redesign the EXISTING homepage pattern, keeping map in the background, "Where to?" input at the top, and a rounded bottom sheet containing services and rider recent history. Keep the arrangement familiar but make it balanced, attractive, spacious and practical.
Composition: ONE large straight-on phone-screen mockup, no device frame, no perspective, nearly fills portrait canvas. Mobile proportional layout around 430x900. Small external label below: "Rider home • Design proposal • Sample routes". Do not make a comparison board.
Layout: safe area top; a white circular hamburger button top-left and white circular outlined sun/theme control top-right. Below them ONE horizontal elevated white search bar, magnifier at left, bold "Where to?" in charcoal, then an inset pale-silver "Schedule" button with a clean calendar outline at right. Modest corner radius18, subtle soft shadow. No brand header, greeting, hero text, wallet balance, statistics, promotional banner or bottom tab bar.
Let the actual map remain clearly visible through approximately the upper 48% of the viewport. A green circular crosshair recenter button floats at the map's lower right, above the sheet. Do not put a map-location marker at a claimed user's real position. This is a visual design example, not a simulated real trip.
Bottom white sheet starts around mid-screen with broad rounded top corners28 and small centered drag handle. Padding22. First row "Our services" at left, small green "Explore" right. Next row THREE EQUAL compact tiles filling the width with equal gaps12. Soft mint/silver surfaces, no heavy border or giant image. Inside each: compact 3D service illustration about52x48, title and one short subtitle: "Ride" / "Everyday trips"; "Courier" / "Send a parcel"; "Schedule" / "Book ahead". All text fully visible; no truncation.
Below, section title "Ride again" and green "See all" right. TWO clean horizontal recent-route rows separated by a faint divider, not bulky nested cards. Small circular mint history-arrow outline at left, destination title and smaller muted origin below, then a clear compact "Ride again" text action plus chevron at right. Use FICTIONAL illustrative route samples, not actual user data: row1 title "Ikeja City Mall", subtitle "From Allen Avenue"; row2 "Lekki Phase 1", subtitle "From Victoria Island". Do not add a status, fare, rating or date. Enough readable space for destinations; 2-line wrap permitted. No cropped or overlapping copy.
At the sheet bottom a slim quiet mint safety strip with shield outline and concise "Safety tools for every trip". This is a link to existing safety tools, not an absolute safety guarantee.
Visual identity: clean white-forward modern Bolt/Uber-inspired mobile design, Rakky Ride forest green #176B17 primary, charcoal #141A14 text, silver #EEF1EC secondary surfaces, pale mint #EAF5E5. Restrained shadows and refined spacing. Outline utility icons consistent stroke2, visual22–24 with48 touch areas. Body text14–16 and section headings20 at430px scale. No harsh gradients, dark panels, extraneous badges, fabricated features or huge artwork. Make all content fit comfortably in the single screen with a clean bottom safe area. Preserve real Google Maps in the eventual app; the design is only an overlay proposal.

Use case: ui-mockup. Edit target: this single Rakky Ride rider homepage proposal. Keep this design, public road-map reference, white rounded bottom sheet, green 3D car, cardboard box, green/white calendar, two recent route rows, same copy and color palette. Make these focused refinements:
1. Move the entire "Where to?" search bar upward so it sits about16 logical pixels below the top circular menu/theme controls, rather than the current large gap. Keep all controls inside safe area.
2. Increase visible map space slightly: bottom sheet begins about43% down the full phone viewport. The map stays the background, no new roads or fake map illustration.
3. Make the three service tiles more COMPACT: each tile about112 logical pixels tall instead of150. Keep equal widths and padding. Reduce the 3D illustrations to about52 logical pixels tall (around110px in this source image), preserving the SAME car, box and calendar appearance. Keep full labels/subtitles readable. Illustration must not dominate card.
4. Keep "Our services" and "Ride again" section headings around20–21 logical pixels, slightly less oversized, still bold. Preserve calm spacing without large blank gaps.
5. Preserve the two history rows, full destination titles, origin subtitles and green "Ride again" actions. Keep safety strip at bottom and comfortable safe area. No new navigation or features.
6. Correct the tiny map copyright text to "Map data ©2026 Google". The app will retain its existing real Google Maps and attribution unchanged.
Do not change the words, replace the icons, introduce branding, add an avatar, invent data or add a bottom navigation bar. One crisp, polished, straight-on mobile page, no frame. This is a design approval image, no code.
